profile.name: Timofey
profile.lead: I build applied web systems for working with data: APIs, PostgreSQL and Redis, interfaces, and the Linux servers they run on. I have used this approach for about three years at the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics.

stats.label: from API and database to production

about: For about three years I have worked on internal services at the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics. I build web interfaces for scientific and operational data, connect them to APIs and databases, configure authorization, and look after the Linux servers that run the applications.
The useful part is seeing the whole system: data shape, backend, a clear interface, PostgreSQL or Redis, then Nginx, systemd, HTTPS, monitoring, and notes for the next person who has to run it.

highlights.title: Practical
highlights.body: The interface solves a concrete job without extra machinery.

highlights.title: Reliable
highlights.body: Validation, access control, health checks, logs, and recovery.

highlights.title: Maintainable
highlights.body: Environment configuration, modular code, and a deployment that can be repeated.

bullets: Internal web applications for viewing, editing, and visualizing scientific and operational data.
REST APIs on FastAPI and Flask, with PostgreSQL, Redis, and several data sources in one application.
Linux deployment: Python environments, frontend builds, Nginx, systemd, HTTPS, and configuration kept out of the repo.
Access through Keycloak/OIDC, JWT checks, and roles for protected operations.
After launch: logs, resource checks, Grafana, health checks, and backups.
Runbooks so a service can be updated and restored without reading the project from scratch.

education.note: A diploma with distinction. The course covered programming, information-system design, and databases; the working projects and Linux administration came after.

projectsLead: Work and personal projects. In each one I owned the integration, configuration, and the environment they run in.

projects.title: db-configs — one interface for several databases
projects.summary: A workspace where a user picks a PostgreSQL source, browses tables, and makes allowed edits without a direct database connection.
bullets: Requests are routed to several PostgreSQL databases from configuration.
Server sessions and rollback of the latest changes in that session.
OIDC via Keycloak, JWT checks, and role-based access.
React SPA and FastAPI, started with Uvicorn, systemd, and Nginx.

projects.title: db-plots — charts from the database
projects.summary: An interface for time series in PostgreSQL: pick channels and a range, compare them on Plotly charts.
bullets: React, TypeScript, Redux Toolkit, and a typed API layer.
Dates, time zones, and selected ranges.
Responsive UI, localization, and a build for an Nginx subpath.

projects.title: redis-grafana — collect, store, watch
projects.summary: Telemetry from a TCP source to dashboards: binary messages are decoded, stored in Redis TimeSeries, and shown in Grafana.
bullets: Async pipeline with queues, backpressure, and reconnects.
Redis TimeSeries aggregation rules for several retention windows.
Flask and React controller for channels, configuration, status, and logs.

projects.title: Keycloak — access deployment
projects.summary: Realms, clients, and roles, then OIDC in the apps: keycloak-js on the frontend and JWT role checks on the API.

opsLead: I prepare Linux servers and keep applications running after launch.

ops.title: Linux base
bullets: Debian and Ubuntu packages and layout
Users, sudo, permissions, SSH keys
Disks, logs, and rotation
Cron and systemd timers

ops.title: Network and security
bullets: Only the ports that are needed
Nginx and Caddy for SPAs and APIs
TLS certificates
Secrets in the environment, dedicated service users

ops.title: Services and data
bullets: systemd restart policy and journalctl
PostgreSQL, Redis, TimescaleDB
Python venv, Uvicorn, Hypercorn
Vite and pnpm frontend builds

ops.title: Operations
bullets: Health checks, logs, memory, and disk
Backups of data and configuration
Grafana and time series
Notes for start, update, and failure
